title: The Sequelae of the Entrenched Misinformations in Schistosomiasis Biology: The Radiation-Attenuated Larva Vaccine
content: Schistosomiasis morbidity and mortality are essentially due to the sequelae of granulomatous inflammation around worms’ eggs trapped in tissues of the mammalian final stage, notably man. Eggs that reach the excreta are the means of pathogen transmission to the snail intermediate stage, responsible for releasing thousands of cercariae. The cercaria with intact head and forked tail is the infective agent for man and animals. Radiation-attenuated (RA) cercariae are able to navigate the epidermis, dermis and the lung capillaries but die therein, and do not access the liver to grow, mate, and start producing eggs. Experimental immunization with RA cercariae consistently elicited remarkable reduction in challenge worm counts and worm egg burden. Ethical and logistic concerns urged the scientific community to select and identify worm-derived subunit antigens, to substitute for the RA cercariae. Numerous Schistosoma-derived molecules were identified, characterized, and prepared as synthetic constructs, recombinant proteins, or plasmid DNA, incorporated into diverse adjuvants, and used for experimental immunization. Several molecules elicited similar or higher levels of protection than the RA vaccine model, up to 80% reduction in challenge worm and worm eggs counts. Like for the RA model, eggs remained in host tissues and excreta to elicit disease, secure transmission, and induce immune responses favorable for reinfection. Thus, vaccination may apparently be of no use for schistosomiasis control. In contrast, severing cercariae tail from head via using water pumps’ pressure as reported by Korir Sisca and Essendi Walter at Egerton University, Kenya may well be the road to elimination of schistosomiasis.
